problem: Existing LLM-based zero-shot VLN agents (NavGPT, DiscussNav) are evaluated on static, discrete, unrealistic R2R environments and ignore environmental feedback (e.g. failed execution due to obstacles). Zero-shot object-nav agents (CoW, ESC) cannot handle complex or abstract instructions.
motivation: Real-world robots face obstacles and pedestrians, so an agent must adjust its plan when execution deviates from expectation. The authors observe that LLM planners can be made adaptive by feeding in-plan and out-of-plan execution feedback, and made more accurate by consulting specialized expert models. No suitable realistic continuous benchmark for multi-task zero-shot instruction following existed, so they also build one.
key_idea: An LLM planner (Vicuna v1.5-13B) that regenerates the remaining plan whenever executing an action produces out-of-plan feedback, aided by instruction-parsing, vision-perception and decision-making experts, evaluated on a new UE5 simulator and NavBench.
insight: Ablations on ObjectNav show each component adds a bit: environmental feedback raises SR 18.5→21.0, trajectory history →22.2, and the decision-making expert →23.4. Removing the instruction parsing expert drops Abstract SR from 36.0 to 27.7, so intent inference matters most when no object is named. Combining image tags and detection beats either alone (23.4 vs 21.0). A stronger LLM (GPT-4 Turbo) improves SR by 6.3 on a 48-instruction subset, so LLM quality is a bottleneck.
method: Instruction Parsing Expert: Vicuna LLM extracts ordered landmarks for step-by-step instructions or infers goal objects for abstract instructions (e.g. 'I am thirsty' -> [water, drink]); its output feeds initial plan generation p=P(I, I(I)).

Vision Perception Expert: RAM++ image tagging on four views (front/left/right/rear) plus Grounding DINO detection; detections are highlighted so the planner trusts reliable objects and ignores tagging noise.
Global actions and planner: LLM planner outputs move_to_object(o), move_to_room(r), move_to_direction(d) or stop(), with trajectory history buffer of observations, thoughts and actions.

Environmental feedback / self-correction: Grounding DINO+SAM+depth localize the target in 3D and the distance to the stopping location is checked against a threshold; success gives in-plan feedback (keep plan), failure gives out-of-plan feedback ('move to o failed') and the planner discards actions from step i onward and re-plans.
Decision-making Expert: a second LLM reviews the planner's thought and action and revises suboptimal actions (e.g. turn left -> move_to_object(shelf)).
Local policy: Fast Marching Method plans a path on an obstacle map to the localized goal; low-level actions are forward 20cm, turn 15°.

NavBench + UE5 simulator: four scenes (restaurant, cafe, nursing room, home), 1,615 GPT-4-generated (and self-refined) instructions over ObjectNav (81), Simple (494), Abstract (278), Step-by-step (762).

setting.backbone: Vicuna v1.5-13B (frozen) for planner and experts; GPT-4 Turbo variant on a subset; RAM++, Grounding DINO, SAM as perception
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D from four views (front/left/right/rear) with agent pose, plus semantic segmentation available in simulator
setting.action_space: high-level move_to_object/room/direction/stop executed via Fast Marching local policy; low-level Move Forward 20cm, Turn Left/Right 15°, Stop
setting.privileged: none (depth and pose used for 3D localization; simulator-provided)

numbers_note: Benchmark is the authors' own NavBench (no official split names; 'test' used as placeholder). No results on R2R/standard benchmarks.
results: CorNav (Vicuna-13B) reaches average SR 28.1 across four NavBench tasks versus 20.5 for the best baseline (ESC with GPT-4 + Grounding DINO), winning on every task, with the largest gain on step-by-step (SR 29.4 vs 20.8 best baseline). With GPT-4 Turbo on a 48-instruction subset SR rises from 20.8 to 27.1.
limitations: Absolute success rates remain low (~28%), and evaluation is only in the authors' own simulator with 4 scenes and GPT-generated instructions; no real-robot or standard VLN benchmark results.
Baselines are adapted object-nav methods rather than other LLM-VLN agents (NavGPT etc.), and GPT-4 comparison is only on a tiny 48-instruction subset.
Relies on privileged-style simulator depth/pose for 3D localization and feedback; heavy multi-model pipeline and repeated LLM calls.
